subject.title: Durable core PR2/6: add optional shared-state foundation

question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned cross-owner durable-runtime schema and public durable configuration now, and if so should this foundation be developed against current main rather than the 2026.7.1 release branch?
rationale: The branch creates a broad new configuration and persisted-state contract rather than repairing an established behavior, while its linked RFC remains open without recorded maintainer acceptance.

options.title: Require RFC approval and retarget
options.body: Keep the PR open, decide the owner boundary in the linked RFC, then retarget an approved and narrowed implementation to current main.

options.title: Narrow to an internal prerequisite
options.body: Remove public durable config and unsupported authority/worker controls, retaining only a maintainer-approved internal seam if one is concretely needed now.

options.title: Decline the shared durable layer
options.body: Close or split the proposal and require any remaining restart, delivery, or lifecycle gaps to be solved by their existing owners.

recommendation.title: Require RFC approval and retarget
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open, decide the owner boundary in the linked RFC, then retarget an approved and narrowed implementation to current main.

likelyOwner.reason: A current-main owner for the shared state database and cross-owner lifecycle boundary should make this architectural decision; the supplied context does not safely identify one.
